skills.name: build

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline

skills.name: troubleshooting

630. static mut INSTANCE: MaybeUninit<Inner> = MaybeUninit::uninit();
631. 
632. /// Whether the frame allocator has been initialized.
633. static INSTANCE_INIT: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
634. 
635. /// Returns a mutable reference to the initialized singleton.
636. //
637. // Trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`): `instance` reads the
638. // module-level `static mut INSTANCE` / `INSTANCE_INIT` through
639. // `unsafe { INSTANCE.assume_init_mut() }`. A Verus `spec fn` cannot read those
640. // statics, and the verifier does not support `static mut` paths, so the bridge
641. // between the live singleton and the uninterpreted `phys_view()` is asserted
642. // here as an external contract: once the allocator is initialized, the returned
643. // reference is well-formed and its abstract view equals `phys_view().frames`.
644. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
645. #[verus_spec(result =>
646.     requires
647.         phys_view().initialized,
648.     ensures
649.         (*result).inv(),
650.         (*result)@ == phys_view().frames,
651. )]
652. fn instance() -> &'static mut Inner {
653.     if unlikely(!INSTANCE_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
654.         panic!("frame allocator used before init()");
655.     }
656. 
657.     // SAFETY: `INSTANCE_INIT` is `true`, so `INSTANCE` has been fully written by `init()`.
658.     // The kernel is single-threaded with interrupts disabled, so no concurrent access is possible.
659.     unsafe { INSTANCE.assume_init_mut() }
660. }
661. 
662. //==================================================================================================
663. // Public Free Functions
664. //==================================================================================================
665. 
666. /// Initialize the frame allocator singleton.
667. ///
668. /// # Safety
669. ///
670. /// Must be called exactly once during boot, before any other function
671. /// in this module.
672. //
673. // Skip/exclude from the proof target (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`): `init`
674. // materializes the `&'static mut [u8]` refcount table from `static mut
675. // REFCOUNT_STORAGE` and writes the `static mut INSTANCE`, neither of which the
676. // verifier supports. Its `#[verus_spec]` contract is honored as a trust boundary.
677. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
678. #[verus_spec(result =>
679.     ensures
680.         // `init` establishes the subsystem invariant. On success the allocator is
681.         // marked initialized; on either outcome the abstract view is well-formed
682.         // (vacuously so if it never became initialized).
683.         phys_view().inv(),
684.         match result {
685.             Ok(()) => phys_view().initialized,
686.             Err(_) => true,
687.         },
688. )]
689. pub(super) unsafe fn init(bitmap: Bitmap) -> Result<(), Error> {
690.     if unlikely(INSTANCE_INIT.load(ORDER)) {
691.         return Err(Error::new(ErrorCode::InvalidArgument, "frame allocator already initialized"));
692.     }
693. 
694.     info!(
695.         "frame allocator: {} frames, {} MB",
696.         bitmap.number_of_bits(),
697.         (bitmap.number_of_bits() * mem::FRAME_SIZE) / constants::MEGABYTE,
698.     );
699. 
700.     let nframes: usize = bitmap.number_of_bits();
701.     if nframes > NFRAMES {
702.         return Err(Error::new(
703.             ErrorCode::InvalidArgument,
704.             "frame bitmap is larger than the configured refcount storage",
705.         ));
706.     }
707. 
708.     // SAFETY: single-threaded boot; no other reference to `REFCOUNT_STORAGE` exists.
709.     let refcount: &'static mut [u8] = unsafe { &mut REFCOUNT_STORAGE[..] };
710. 
711.     // Defensively sync refcounts with any bits already set in the incoming bitmap. The
712.     // current microvm boot path supplies an empty bitmap and performs all reservations
713.     // via `book()` / `alloc_range()` after `init()`, so this loop normally does nothing.
714.     // It is kept as a safety net so a future boot path that hands us a pre-populated
715.     // bitmap (for example to express firmware-reserved regions) does not silently end
716.     // up with `bitmap bit = 1, refcount = 0`, which would cause the first `free()` of
717.     // such a frame to be rejected as a spurious double-free.
718.     for (i, slot) in refcount.iter_mut().enumerate().take(nframes) {
719.         if matches!(bitmap.test(i), Ok(true)) {
720.             *slot = 1;
721.         }
722.     }
723.
